html:
Livingstonia was the mission of the Free Church of Scotland founded in 1875 on Lake Malawi in memory of David Livingstone, and later moved to a plateau in the north, where it built a famous school.

A year later the Church of Scotland founded Blantyre in the south, named after Livingstone's birthplace. Both fought the slave trade, opened schools and preached, and their presence led Britain to declare a protectorate in 1891 to keep the Portuguese out.

Mission schools such as the Overtoun Institution at Livingstonia trained clerks, teachers and pastors who went to work across southern Africa, and many early nationalists, including John Chilembwe in his own way, came out of this world. Christianity became the faith of most Malawians, following Livingstone.
